ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the graph of the linear function $y=3x-3$ intersects the $x$-axis at point $A$, and intersects the graph of the direct proportion function $y=kx$ at point $B(a, 3)$. Taking point $A$ as the center and the length of $AB$ as the radius, an arc is drawn that intersects the $x$-axis at point $C$. Please directly write down the coordinates of point $C$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} From the problem statement, we have $y=3x-3$. When $y=0$, it follows that $3x-3=0$, which solves to: $x=1$. Therefore, $A(1, 0)$ and hence $\left|AB\right|=\sqrt{(3-0)^2+(2-1)^2}=\sqrt{10}$. Draw an arc with point $A$ as the center and the length of $AB$ as the radius, intersecting the x-axis at point $C$. Therefore, $C\left(\sqrt{10}+1, 0\right)$ or $\left(-\sqrt{10}+1, 0\right)$. Hence, the coordinates of point $C$ are $\boxed{C\left(\sqrt{10}+1, 0\right)}$ or $\boxed{C\left(-\sqrt{10}+1, 0\right)}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, with the x-axis horizontal to the right and the y-axis vertical upward, and the origin is labeled O. The steeper oblique straight line intersects the positive half-axis of the x-axis at point A, and in the first quadrant intersects another oblique straight line passing through the origin at point B; point B is labeled near the upper intersection point of the two oblique lines. The figure does not clearly draw point C or the arc, so it cannot be uniquely judged from the image whether C is on the left side or the right side of A. Reasoning: The y-coordinate of point B is 3, and B is on the line y=3x-3, so 3=3a-3, solving gives a=2, therefore B=(2,3). Point A is the intersection point of the line y=3x-3 and the x-axis. Let y=0, get 0=3x-3, so x=1, that is A=(1,0). The radius AB=√[(2-1)^2+(3-0)^2]=√10. If C is on the x-axis, let C=(x,0), and AC=AB=√10, then |x-1|=√10, so x=1+√10 or x=1-√10. Since the figure does not explicitly specify which side only the arc takes, both kinds of intersection points hold.
